findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the repository can retrieve these long-lived static credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the function's environment variables (which contain secrets) are protected only by the default service-owned key and are readable in plain text by any principal able to describe the function.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS or Node.js upstream, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-verified; tampering with the artefact between build and deployment would go undetected.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC and its egress traffic cannot be restricted by security groups or network layering, removing a control against data exfiltration.
